answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce resource before its vote or trade counts, and the protocol caps how much influence one escrow can buy. A newcomer can create a thousand identities, but cannot multiply the weight of a fixed deposit; splitting it only spreads the same influence across accounts. The attacker therefore has to lock up real capital for long enough to matter, accepting opportunity cost and possible slashing for proven fraud. Even pigment, juniper, and zenith cannot turn cheap names into costly stake.
